title: GPU warmstart whispering journal — observational runbook draft
content:
Context and purpose:
This is a working observational journal and runbook sketch for a recurring low-noise GPU instability pattern we've been seeing during node warmstarts. I coined the shorthand 'whispering' because the errors are subtle (short ECC-correctable bursts + a transient nvlink negotiation hiccup) and often precede a driver oops or a delayed kernel panic by 10–30 minutes under light load. This doc captures raw observations from nightshift, quick diagnostic steps we tried, and hypotheses/experiments to prioritize.

Summary of recent behavior (synthesis):
- Affected fleet: gpu-pool-edge-2 and gpu-pool-spotty-4 (NVIDIA A100 80GB, mixed firmware).
- Symptom sequence (typical): warmstart -> ECC correctable burst on GPU X -> nvlink peer 0 reports negotiation timeout -> driver logs an 'rmh' WARN then an oops in nvidia_uvm (rare) -> node becomes slow/unresponsive for ~5–15m -> either auto-recovery or kernel panic requiring hard reboot.
- Load context: mostly occurs during low-util warmstarts (model container spins up with minimal tokens), and often within 3–12 minutes of startup.

What we observed in logs (representative snippets):
- dmesg/timestamps: "[2028-02-09T03:11:42Z] gpu0: ecc correctable burst count 23 -> rate spike"
- nvlink: "NVLINK: peer 1 negotiation timeout, fallback to single-link"
- driver: "nvidia: WARN rmh: unexpected fence wait 0x3a"
- klog (rare): "kernel: BUG: unable to handle kernel NULL pointer dereference at 0x0 in nvidia_uvm"

Nightshift quick actions and immediate observations:
- Soft reboot of container (docker restart) often allowed workload to resume; underlying node sometimes recovered without intervention.
- When we bumped the node's GPU power limit down by 5% during a warmstart, one occurrence did NOT progress to kernel oops; possible thermal/power negotiation sensitivity.
- Disabling early NVSwitch probing (sysctl hack we tried) delayed the nvlink negotiation and in 2/3 attempts avoided the follow-on driver fault.

Hypotheses (prioritized):
1) Persistent micro-power/voltage drift during early warmstart causes increased ECC correctable rates and confuses nvlink negotiation (timing sensitive).
2) A firmware/driver interaction at initialization leaves the NVLink fabric briefly in a partial state; if a specific sequence of IPC operations (UVM mappings, peer-to-peer checks) happens quickly, it triggers an unstable code path in the driver.
3) KV cache warm-prime causing specific kernel/driver ordering that surfaces a race in the nvidia_uvm callbacks.

Immediate diagnostic checklist for oncall (short, actionable):
- When pager fires: collect snapshots immediately (timestamp in UTC):
  1) kubectl -n infra logs --since=30m --tail=200 <pod> 
  2) ssh node && sudo dmesg -T | tail -n 200 > /tmp/dmesg-snippet.txt
  3) sudo nvidia-smi -q -d ECC,POWER,INFO > /tmp/nv-smi.txt
  4) sudo cat /proc/driver/nvidia/version > /tmp/nvidia-ver.txt
  5) svc-restart: do NOT immediately reboot node — attempt container-level restart first and observe 10m.
- Short rubric: if ECC correctable bursts > 50 in 10m AND nvlink negotiation messages present => cordon node and escalate to SRE lead.

Quick remediation steps we trialed (and notes):
- soft-restart container (low blast radius): often recovers.
- set kernel parameter "nvidia_nvlink_delayed_init=1" (experiment flag) to force nvlink init after driver probe; reduced occurrences in limited A/B. TODO: formalize as feature flag in infra PR.
- conservative power limit tweak (95% rated) during warmstart window: promising but not yet safe fleet-wide.

Runbook draft (warmstart-whisper recovery):
1) Detect pattern: automated telemetry rule (SLO): ECC_correctable_rate spike + nvlink-neg msg within 15m of node boot.
2) Auto-action: cordon node -> route new model uploads away -> keep existing in-flight if under 30s TTL.
3) Try soft mitigation: restart model container(s) touching GPU; if containers restart cleanly and no kernel oops after 15m, uncordon.
4) If driver WARN/oops or kernel panic observed -> escalate to 'firmware-driver' incident path and schedule hard reboot window with kernel crash dump capture.
5) For recurring nodes: mark for firmware reflash + run retest harness (see linked artifacts).

Planned experiments (next sprint):
- Telemetry: add a short-lived probe that records the sequence of NVLink state transitions at boot (small kernel module / eBPF probe) to capture ordering without heavy overhead.
- Infra: land infra PR to add a 30s delayed nvlink init flag at node startup (feature-gate controlled).
- Test fleet: pick 20 canary nodes across two racks; test delayed-init, reduced power-limit, and aggressive retry backoff; run model warmstart frequency sim to try and repro.

Outstanding questions (open for engineering research):
- Is the ECC burst a symptom or the root cause? We need per-GPU voltage/telemetry correlation (PMU) during warmstart.
- Firmware matrix: which exact GPU firmware versions correlate? Our device inventory has partial tagging — need full flash manifest.
- Are certain model containers performing a pattern of UVM mapping that deterministically triggers the driver race?

Ownership and immediate next steps:
- Maya Chen (SRE): owner of this doc, coordinate small experiment and infra PR.
- Priya Iyer (Platform): prototype delayed-nvlink-init gate.
- Liam O'Connor (Infra): pick 20 canary nodes and implement test harness for warmstart churn.
- Diego Martinez (Applied ML / model infra): create a minimal repro workload that exercises UVM/peer-to-peer path.

Notes to self / oncall heuristics (raw):
- When in doubt, leave node cordoned for 30m after fixing — we saw 2nd-chance panics after 8–12m.
- Add a metric: nvlink_negotiation_retries{node} to Grafana.
- Slack huddle channel: #sre-gpu-whisper (temporary until resolution).

Reference links and artifacts:
- Investigation ticket: SRE-4821 (see linked_artifacts).
- Infra PR with delayed-init prototype: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/911
- Raw crash logs bucket: gs://redwood-sre/gpu-whisper-logs/2028-02/

Appendix: short copy-paste checklist for responders (one-line commands)
- Collect logs: scp node:/tmp/dmesg-snippet.txt . && scp node:/tmp/nv-smi.txt .
- Probe nvlink state: sudo nvidia-smi nvlink --query -l 10 --format=csv | tail -n 50
- Soft restart container: kubectl -n models rollout restart deployment/<deploy-name>

This is intentionally informal — add notes and corrections here. We will formalize into a runbook and a pager playbook once experiments validate a reliable mitigation path.
